name: us-large-cap/large-cap-sleeve-blend
title: Large-cap sleeve blend — residual momentum + PIT quality + filing-text similarity + short S&P additions
description: Four economically unrelated, beta-neutral S&P 500 single-name sleeves summed at fixed inverse-IS-vol multipliers (10 % IS vol): Blitz-Huij-Martens residual 12-1 momentum (0.457), a point-in-time EDGAR XBRL quality/payout composite (2.478), YoY 10-K/10-Q text similarity 'non-changers' (2.664), and a 5-session short of each new S&P 500 addition against its sector (1.211). Books reset at NYSE month-ends, hedges daily, REC on event days.
direction: long/short single-name book, beta-neutral (beta -0.00 to the EW member market), net dollars avg +0.30 (range -0.09 to +0.91), gross avg 4.44 / max 6.29

backtest.cost_type: 5 bp per side all-in on sum|dw| at weight level (hedges, vol scaling and REC baskets included); price returns, no financing, borrow or short rebate

live_notes: SIM book: every leg fills at the yfinance daily close from the shared data/ cache (fee 5 bp, slippage 0 = the research's 5 bp/side all-in). No order book, no borrow cost or locate, no short rebate, no margin interest on a 4.4x-gross book. Much weaker evidence than a venue fill; a real account would pay borrow and financing that the backtest and this track both omit.

Drift cost: the research holds weights constant between rebalances at no cost; the live book re-targets every name to its weight every session and pays 5 bp on that drift turnover too, so live costs run somewhat above the 42x/yr the report charges.

Open universe: the S&P 500 changes monthly, so the broker is SimPortfolioBroker(open_universe=True). `symbols` here is the member list at deploy; new additions join the ledger when they get a weight, and a flat leg that left the index is dropped at the next restart. `bar_key` is NOT min-over-legs: it is the latest SPY session that >= 98 % of current members have printed. Until then the daemon waits and re-checks every 30 min.

Gross cap 6.3 = the validated maximum (6.29 in the PR; 6.31 on refreshed data 2026-09-27, so it can bind by ~0.2 % on an extreme day). A `scaled_by` in the journal means the book is at the edge of what was tested.

Live data, all by the research's own fetchers, via `runner.py --fetch <name>`: Wikipedia membership/changes every 6 h -> data/us-large-cap-live/ (NOT the tracked code/us-large-cap/shared/ CSVs, which stay at the research snapshot); prices for members + held + still-printing panel names via fetch_universe.py --refresh; fetch_actions, fetch_xbrl --refresh, fetch_filing_text --update once per traded bar (~6 min in total). EDGAR raw caches live in data/SP500_edgar/ (seeded from /tmp). The runner refuses to trade if any EDGAR output is > 7 days old. No refresh happens 09:00-17:00 New York on weekdays.

REC dependency: an addition is shorted at the close of its first session in the index only if Wikipedia's 'Historical components' table lists it by then. Wikipedia is normally edited on the announcement, but if a change lands late the short is missed or entered late.

Flatten: with ~500 legs, the dashboard's flatten rebuilds the book via broker_from_meta with YahooQuotes (1 h cache), which may re-download every leg and hit the 90 s timeout. It fails without writing anything. To flatten for real, stop the daemon and run the FLATTEN_SRC snippet from harness/dashboard.py by hand, right after a data refresh.
Upkeep: code/us-large-cap/shared/trading_calendar.py NYSE_HOLIDAYS ends 2027 and must be extended yearly or month-end rebalances next to holidays are mis-timed.

Known research-data caveats (non-blocking): panel.py masks a name one bar BEFORE a >50 % daily move (bad.shift(-1)) and drops tickers with >= 3 such bars over the full sample. That is look-ahead in the backtest, but only 24 name-days since 2011 on kept tickers, and it cannot fire on the live last bar. The FISV->FI alias leaves Fiserv without prices, so it is absent from the backtest and from this book.

Deploy check 2026-09-27: runner --check on bar 2026-09-25 matches an independent blend_weights recompute on the same live universe exactly (max|diff| 0; gross 4.715, net +0.414, 501 names). The largest legs are REC shorts on the 2026-09-21 additions P (-0.298) and ILMN (-0.297), on their 5th and last session (cover at the 2026-09-28 close); the largest stock-book leg is FICO +0.035. The PR saves no weight series, so no lag test was possible; convention per spec: row t is decided at close t and filled at close t.
